{{spoiler|''[[Guild Wars Prophecies|Prophecies]]'', ''[[Guild Wars Eye of the North|Eye of the North]]'', and ''[[Guild Wars Beyond|Beyond]]''}} {{NPC infobox | name = Gwen | type = Human | image = [[File:Gwen (Eye of the North).jpg|200px]] | affiliation = Ebon Vanguard | profession = me | service = Hero | level = 1, 20 | campaign = Prophecies | campaign2 = Eye of the North | campaign3 = Beyond | map1 = [[File:Gwen wallpaper.jpg|200px]] | map1-text = A wallpaper featuring Gwen. }}{{TOCright}} {{Quotation|eye of the north|Born in [[Ascalon]], Gwen has witnessed horrible things in her young life, seeing both her country and family destroyed by the [[Charr]]. After [[the Searing]], she was captured and enslaved by the Charr, but escaped and fled north, where she found other human exiles. Since then, Gwen has become an adventurer. She makes her home in the [[Eye of the North (outpost)|Eye of the North]], the headquarters of the [[Ebon Vanguard]], where she serves [[Captain Langmar]]. She is one of the fiercest defenders of Ascalon, determined to exact vengeance against those who destroyed her home. Gwen has survived on the edges of Charr territory for years, watching them tear apart her childhood dreams and her beautiful homeland. Now she has nothing but memories—and anger—to sustain her. She is not the girl she once was...}} {{quotation|[https://www.guildwars.com/heartsofthenorth/ official website]|The charr destroyed everything dear to her when Gwen was a young girl. Her toughness and single-minded hatred of the charr served her well as a member of the Ebon Vanguard, but Gwen was bitter and full of rage – until she met Keiran Thackeray. The noble ranger was immune to her cruelest barbs and took her indifference in stride, and over time Gwen's frozen heart melted. She finally realized her true feelings for Keiran when he was reported missing in action. Now Gwen leads the Ebon Vanguard alone and waits for any word of Keiran’s fate...}} [[Gwen|Gwen]] (born 1060 [[Mouvelian calendar|AE]]) is an Ascalonian adventurer and the current commanding officer of the Ebon Vanguard. Originally hailing from [[Ashford]], she lived with her mother [[Sarah]] until [[the Searing]], when her mother was killed and she was taken captive by the Charr. For seven years she suffered at their hands, during which time she developed a deep hatred of the feline race. Eventually, she escaped, fleeing north until she chanced upon an Ebon Vanguard camp, where Captain Langmar took her in. Within a year she had risen to the position of second-in-command, and aided in the effort to rescue Langmar and her soldiers from the [[Charr Homelands]] when they were captured during a mission. In doing so, she helped topple [[Hierophant Burntsoul]], which was the main stepping stone for [[Pyre Fierceshot]]'s long road to revolution. Alongside Langmar and others, she followed the Vanguard to victory in the battle against [[the Great Destroyer]]. Other notable accomplishments at this stage of her life include helping to stop a possible [[Titan]] threat in the Charr Homelands and returning to Ascalon to deal with [[Dahgar, the Eye of Flame]], one of her Charr tormentors during her long years in captivity. By 1079 AE, she had become romantically involved with [[Keiran Thackeray|Lieutenant Keiran Thackeray]]. However, her cold personality made his advances difficult and eventually he gave up, deciding to travel to [[Kryta]] with his unit, the [[Ebon Falcons]], in order to help defeat the [[White Mantle]] in return for aid against the Charr from the Krytan monarchy. During the [[Krytan civil war]], Captain Langmar was killed and Keiran was reported as missing in action, leaving a distraught Gwen in command of the Ebon Vanguard. She organized a search for Keiran, eventually reuniting with him at [[Anvil Rock]]. After the two reunited, Keiran proposed, and the two were [[the Wedding|married]] in [[Olafstead (explorable area)|Olafstead]]. In 1080 AE, [[King Adelbern]] recalls Gwen and the Ebon Vanguard to fortify [[Ebonhawke]], a town alongside the [[Blazeridge Mountains]], in order to solidify supply lines to [[Ascalon City]]. 4 of 4 ==Notes== [[File:"Gwen Final" concept art.jpg|thumb|200px|Concept art by Kristen Perry, claimed to be for ''[[Guild Wars Utopia]]'']] *Gwen will follow the player nearly anywhere in pre-Searing Ascalon, if you have won her favor and have no active Gwen-specific tasks. If you have given her a [[flute]], she will periodically heal you for 20 health. *{{bug|It is possible that she stops following the player and while you can talk to her to give her more flowers or another flute, it's not possible to get her to follow you again.}} *Talking to Gwen for the first time after [[The First Vision]] will cause her to give you a [[Monumental Tapestry]]. *Taking Gwen to [[the Underworld]] will trigger a unique [[The Underworld#Dialogue|dialogue]] with her mother, Sarah. Bringing Keiran Thackeray along would trigger a different dialogue with Sarah. *If you take Gwen to the [[Gwen's garden|small grassy area]] behind the [[Eye of the North (outpost)|Eye of the North]], she will talk of her nostalgia for Red Iris Flowers. *A duplicate Gwen will show up as a "Vanguard Mesmer". *Gwen's default weapons are a [[customize]]d max damage [[Item rarity|blue]] 9 Inspiration [[requirement]] [[Crystal Wand]] with [[HCT]] 20% Inspiration Magic and a max energy blue 9 Inspiration requirement [[Jeweled Chalice]] with 20% chance +1 Inspiration Magic. *Gwen has two [[Miniature|miniatures]]: a [[Miniature Gwen|pre-searing version]], and a [[Gwen Doll|doll version]]. *As with most heroes, she has a [[Everlasting Gwen Tonic|tonic form]]. ==Trivia== {{gw2w|Gwen Thackeray}} *The voice actress for this character is [[w:Kari Wahlgren|Kari Wahlgren]], who also voices [[Tahlkora]] and [[Shahai the Cunning]] in ''Nightfall''. *"[[Gwen-chan]]" and "[[Dr. Boar]]" had a tutorial section on the official Japanese site. *To end one of the beta weekend events, Gwen appeared and used [[Spontaneous Combustion]] to wipe out the player population. This is not considered part of Guild Wars [[lore]]; developers often use similar devices to end events. *The official acronym for ''Guild Wars Eye of the North'' is GW:EN, which can be assumed to be intentional allusion to Gwen's name. ;Lore: *Gwen was missing and presumed dead following [[the Searing]]. Over the years, hints of her survival were placed in-game: Gwen's Broken Flute can be found in [[Old Ascalon]], and a Preserved Red Iris Flower can be found in a chest on the [[Barbarous Shore]]. Additionally, a [[Tattered Girl's Cape]] used to spawn in [[Stingray Strand]]. Her fate was first revealed with the release of ''Eye of the North'', and later expanded upon in the Bonus Mission Pack. ;Dialogue: :Several of Gwen's combat and ambient dialogue lines reference various popular films: *"...and I'm all out of mossgum." parodies [[wikiquote:They_Live#John_Nada|a line]] from ''[[w:They Live|They Live]]''. *"If it bleeds, we can kill it." is [[wikiquote:Predator_(film)#Dialogue|a direct quote]] from ''[[w:Predator (film)|Predator]]''. *"The light that burns twice as bright burns half as long." and "You've got some really nice toys there." are both [[wikiquote:Blade Runner|lines of dialogue]] in ''[[w:Blade Runner|Blade Runner]]''. *"Time to die" is the last line of both Leon Kowalski and Roy Batty in ''Blade Runner''. *"Painful to live in fear isn't it?" is another of Leon Kowalski's lines from ''Blade Runner'', during his fight with Deckard. *"It's not an easy thing to meet your maker" is yet another of Roy Batty's lines from ''Blade Runner'', when he meets Eldon Tyrell. *"My mother? Let me tell you about my mother" is also from ''Blade Runner'', said by Leon Kowalski as he shoots Dave Holden. *"Forgiveness? That's Lyssa's job. It's mine to arrange the meeting" paraphrases [[wikiquote:Man_on_Fire_(2004_film)#Dialogue|a line]] from ''[[w:Man on Fire (2004 film)|Man on Fire]]''. **The line in the film itself is a reference to a popular quote [https://www.snopes.com/fact-check/norman-conquest/ misattributed] to Norman Schwarzkopf. *The "stop touching me" quote may be a reference to several Orc Grunt and Peon quotes from Warcraft 2 and 3 which they say in response to being clicked on. *"My name is Gwen. And I don't like yooou" is a likely reference to a line of a doll named Talking Tina in a Twilight Zone episode, who speaks outside of her programmed responses to the father, who does not like the doll. *"The roof, the roof, the roof is on fire" and "We need no water, let the..." are likely a reference to the frequently sampled and covered 1984 hip hop song The Roof Is on Fire by Rock Master Scott & the Dynamic Three; owing to the strong language used in the song's lyrics, the second quote ends in "...". *"Burn baby burn!" is from the 1976 The Trammps song Disco Inferno. *"Ashes, ashes, you all fall down!" is clear reference to the nursery rhyme Ring a Ring O'Roses. {{Heroes nav}} {{featured article}} [[Category:Prophecies quest givers]] [[Category:Eye of the North quest givers]] [[Category:Beyond quest givers]] [[Category:Significant figures]] [[Category:Gwen|*]]
